statement: For every real rounding model M and finite binary tree T of pairs of real numbers, if (d+1)u < 1, where d is the tree depth and u is the model error parameter, the recursively rounded sum of individually rounded leaf products equals the exact sum of a tree of perturbed exact leaf products with the same shape. Each exact product x is replaced by a real y with |y-x| <= ((d+1)u/(1-(d+1)u))|x|. The perturbations concern products, and do not assert perturbations of their individual factors.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct_exists_perturbation
targets.statement: For every model M and every T in Tree(R x R), put u = M.u and d = depth(T). Here Tree(A) consists of finite ordered binary trees generated by leaf(a) for a in A and node(L,R), with no empty tree; depth(leaf(a)) = 0 and depth(node(L,R)) = 1 + max(depth(L),depth(R)). A model consists of u in R with 0 <= u and r: R -> R satisfying: for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z) = z(1+delta). If (d+1)u < 1, then there exists P in Tree(R) such that IsPerturbation(gamma(d+1,u), exactProductTree(T), P) and exactSum(P) = roundedDotProduct(M,T). For k in N and u in R, gamma(k,u) = ku/(1-ku), with k cast to R; d+1 is likewise cast to R in the hypothesis. The relation IsPerturbation(b,X,P) requires exactly the same ordered tree shape and, at every corresponding leaf x of X and y of P, |y-x| <= b|x|; its node rule requires this same relation with the same b on both corresponding subtrees. The function exactSum returns the value at a leaf and adds the exact sums of both children at a node. Thus, writing the leaf labels of T as (a_i,b_i), indexed by their positions i, the theorem asserts that there are real y_i, arranged as leaves of a tree P of exactly the shape of T, with |y_i-a_i b_i| <= ((d+1)u/(1-(d+1)u))|a_i b_i| for every leaf i, and with the exact real sum of all y_i equal to the scalar computed by roundedDotProduct(M,T). That scalar is obtained by rounding each exact leaf product and then rounding each internal addition in the given tree. The uniform bound uses the maximum depth plus one, including for leaves at smaller depths. The hypothesis guarantees a positive denominator.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree
constructions.description: A function Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R). It replaces each leaf (a,b), a,b in R, by the exact real product ab and preserves every ordered internal node: E(leaf((a,b))) = leaf(ab), and E(node(L,R)) = node(E(L),E(R)). It performs no additions and does not choose or balance the tree. The target theorem uses this constructed tree as the reference for the perturbation relation.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree
constructions.description: A function Model -> Tree(R x R) -> Tree(R). For any model M with rounding function r: R -> R, it replaces each leaf (a,b) by r(ab), using Model.mul(M,a,b) = r(ab), and preserves every ordered internal node: Q_M(leaf((a,b))) = leaf(r(ab)), and Q_M(node(L,R)) = node(Q_M(L),Q_M(R)). It does not round the two factors separately or perform additions. This is the tree passed to roundedSum in the construction appearing in the target theorem.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct
constructions.description: A function Model -> Tree(R x R) -> R, defined by roundedDotProduct(M,T) = roundedSum(M,roundedProductTree(M,T)). On real-labelled trees, roundedSum(M,leaf(v)) = v and roundedSum(M,node(L,R)) = r(roundedSum(M,L)+roundedSum(M,R)), because Model.add(M,x,y) = r(x+y). Consequently D_M(leaf((a,b))) = r(ab) and D_M(node(L,R)) = r(D_M(L)+D_M(R)). It rounds each exact product once and each internal addition once in the original ordered binary tree. Encountering a leaf in roundedSum performs no extra rounding. A leaf at depth h passes through one product rounding and h additions. The target theorem equates this scalar with the exact sum of a same-shaped tree whose leaves satisfy the relative bound against exactProductTree(T).

assumptions: The theorem quantifies universally over all models M and all finite nonempty ordered binary trees T of pairs of real numbers. There is no balance requirement, fixed leaf count, sign restriction, or nonzero-factor hypothesis. Internal nodes have exactly two children.

Model membership includes u in R with u >= 0 and a function r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z) = z(1+delta). The error delta may depend on z. Model addition and multiplication apply r to the exact real sum or product.

The explicit additional hypothesis is (depth(T)+1)u < 1, with the natural depth plus one cast to a real. Combined with u >= 0, it gives 0 <= u < 1/(depth(T)+1) and makes the denominator in gamma(depth(T)+1,u) positive.

All factors, intermediate values, perturbed leaf values, and error parameters are real numbers. Depth and the gamma index are natural numbers. The existentially quantified perturbed object is a real-labelled tree, and the perturbation relation enforces the same ordered shape as the exact product tree.
The perturbation bound is uniform over corresponding leaf products. A zero exact leaf product must have zero perturbed value. No perturbation of either individual factor is asserted.

No particular finite floating-point format, representable-value set, or rounding-to-nearest rule is specified. The model rounding property is global on all real inputs; there are no separate overflow or underflow hypotheses.
